need: Help a new executive onboard and understand the organization's operating rhythm.

cases.text: A concise decision-making map of the leadership team and their weekly cadence.
A one-page org chart with the operating rhythm and meeting norms.
A walkthrough deck of the quarterly planning cycle and key stakeholders.
An arrival guide listing first-month milestones and who to meet.
A list of the company's recurring rituals and how decisions are made.
A summary of the new executive's first 90 days checklist.
A generic brochure about the tourism board of a distant region.
A recipe collection for regional desserts.
A car maintenance schedule for a delivery fleet.
A museum annual report from a city far away.
A football club season ticket policy.
A knitting pattern archive with seasonal yarn reviews.
A published note confirming the new process reduced onboarding time by 30%.
A signed statement from the VP that the rhythm is now weekly.
A data snapshot showing first-month completion rate across prior hires.
An email from the CFO verifying the quarterly planning calendar.
A meeting artifact signed by the team lead listing the milestones.
A verified announcement that the executive onboarding program exists.
An unverified rumour about a closure in another industry.
A photo of a beach holiday with no names or dates.
A blog post that guesses the product roadmap without sources.
A meme about Monday meetings generally.
A comment that 'things used to be different' with no evidence.
A horoscope text with a vague forecast.
A physical copy of the leadership operating manual with tabs.
The annual planning workbook used by previous executives.
A printed calendar of this year's leadership forums.
A binder of the onboarding program materials from last cohort.
A slide deck from the last strategy offsite.
A laminated one-pager of the decision rights matrix.
A snow globe from a gift shop.
An old phone charger found in a drawer.
A ticket stub from a concert two years ago.
A coffee mug with a logo of an airline.
A postcard from a resort.
A set of crayons from a child's desk.
